title: Eigenvalue formulation of Stochastic Inflation and application to large perturbation generating inflationary features
summary: Stochastic inflation is a powerful technique for calculating the probability distribution function (PDF) of large inflationary perturbations, which may collapse to form Primordial Black Holes. The PDF, $P({\cal N})$, of the stochastic number of e-folds, ${\cal N}$, satisfies an adjoint Fokker-Planck Equation. We develop a new self-contained eigenvalue technique which can be used to determine $P({\cal N})$. First we apply this method to the simple case of quantum diffusion along a flat potential without any classical drift. We recover the expression for the PDF that has previously been found using characteristic functions, with an exponential tail. We also identify an intermediate regime between the peak and the exponential tail of the PDF, which has not been emphasized in earlier studies, where it exhibits a power-law behaviour, $P({\cal N}) \propto {\cal N}^{-3/2}$. Finally we apply the method to constant drift inflation, in the narrow- and broad-well limits. In the narrow-well limit, there is an analytic solution and the PDF is similar to the drift-free case, with a mildly suppressed tail. In the broad-well limit, determining the full set of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions requires a piecewise construction of the spectrum, and the broad-well PDF is qualitatively different, with an enhanced peak and a strongly suppressed tail.

AI.tldr: A novel eigenvalue method is proposed to solve the stochastic inflation PDF problem, recovering known results and exposing new intermediate power-law behavior and different PDF shapes depending on the inflationary potential's characteristics.
AI.motivation: To calculate the probability distribution function (PDF) of large inflationary perturbations important for Primordial Black Hole formation using a more efficient and self-contained method.
AI.method: A new eigenvalue technique is developed to solve the adjoint Fokker-Planck Equation governing the PDF of the stochastic number of e-folds, applied to various inflationary scenarios including flat potential quantum diffusion and constant drift cases.
AI.result: The new method successfully reproduces known PDFs with exponential tails, discovers an intermediate power-law regime, and reveals distinct PDF behaviors in narrow- and broad-well constant drift scenarios, including analytic solutions and piecewise spectral constructions.
AI.conclusion: The eigenvalue technique provides a robust and versatile tool to determine the PDF of inflationary perturbations under different stochastic inflation settings, highlighting novel regimes and different statistical features of the distributions relevant to Primordial Black Hole formation.

title: 21cmEMUv3: a hybrid diffusion-LSTM emulator of 21cmFAST summary observables
summary: We are witnessing a surge in observations of the cosmic dawn (CD) and epoch of reionisation (EoR), driving an increasing demand for fast and robust theoretical interpretation frameworks. In response, machine learning (ML), and emulation in particular, has emerged as a powerful approach to accelerate and enhance inference pipelines. In this work, we present 21cmEMUv3, an emulator trained on 21cmFASTv3 simulations that model both atomically and molecularly cooling galaxies. 21cmEMUv3 is conditioned on $σ_8$ and ten astrophysical parameters to produce seven summary observables: (i) the cylindrical 21cm power spectrum (PS), emulated for the first time at such high resolution and accuracy across a wide redshift range of $z \sim$ 6--30; (ii) the spherically-averaged 21cm PS; (iii) the mean neutral fraction of the intergalactic medium (IGM); (iv) the mean 21cm spin temperature; (v) the global 21cm signal; (vi) the ultraviolet (UV) luminosity functions (LFs); and (vii) the Thomson scattering optical depth. Notably, the cylindrical 21cm PS is emulated via score-based diffusion, while the remaining six summaries are emulated via long-short term memory (LSTM) networks, all achieving sub-percent median accuracy. We use the emulator to reinterpret current 21cm PS upper limits from HERA, for the first time using state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations to inform priors on star formation inside molecularly cooling galaxies. We find that our inferred soft-band X-ray luminosity per unit star formation rate is consistent with extrapolations of high-mass X-ray binaries to the low-metallicity regimes expected in the first galaxies, excluding values below $10^{39.2}$ erg s$^{-1}M^{-1}_\odot \rm{yr}$ at $95\%$ confidence. Finally, we produce forecasts for the detection of the cosmic 21cm PS with the Square Kilometre Array for different array configurations. The 21cmEMU package is publicly available.

AI.tldr: This work introduces 21cmEMUv3, a high-accuracy emulator based on 21cmFASTv3 simulations, that models seven key 21cm observables relevant to cosmic dawn and reionisation. Using advanced ML techniques, it achieves sub-percent accuracy, informs astrophysical parameter constraints from current data, and delivers forecasts for the Square Kilometre Array. The software is publicly available.
AI.motivation: There is an increasing demand for fast and robust theoretical frameworks to interpret observations of the cosmic dawn and epoch of reionisation, driven by growing data availability.
AI.method: The authors develop 21cmEMUv3, an emulator trained on 21cmFASTv3 simulations conditioned on cosmological and astrophysical parameters, using score-based diffusion to emulate the cylindrical 21cm power spectrum and LSTM networks for six other summary observables.
AI.result: 21cmEMUv3 achieves sub-percent median accuracy across seven key summary observables, enables reinterpretation of current 21cm power spectrum limits with improved priors informed by hydrodynamical simulations, constrains the soft-band X-ray luminosity, and produces detection forecasts for the Square Kilometre Array. The emulator package is publicly released.
AI.conclusion: The 21cmEMUv3 emulator provides a fast, accurate, and versatile tool for theoretical interpretation of cosmic dawn and epoch of reionisation observations, improving parameter inference and enabling robust forecasts for future 21cm cosmology experiments.

title: The sound of dynamical dark energy and modified gravity
summary: Different candidate models are able to reproduce the dynamical dark energy signal preferred by combinations of recent distance measurements. These models may be distinguished by the behavior of their perturbations, which are controlled by the effective sound speed $c_s^2(k,a)$. To explore correlations between the dark energy sound speed and perturbative behavior, we test modified gravity (MG) scenarios in which the dark energy equation of state and sound speed determine modifications to the clustering of matter. We investigate the impact of varying the dark energy sound speed on several cosmological quantities in both General Relativity (GR) and MG. We constrain the dark energy and modified gravity parameters using measurements of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) from Planck PR4, type Ia supernova luminosity distances (SN) from Pantheon+, Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) from DESI DR2, and cosmic shear from DES-Y3. Using the combination of CMB+BAO+SN, we find that, in the MG scenarios, the preference for dynamical dark energy is correlated with deviations from GR over redshifts $z < 2$ at over 95\% confidence level. The significance of these deviations is not degraded when considering a dynamical or superluminal sound speed, but vanishes if we assume a cosmological constant. The inclusion of cosmic shear and CMB lensing data significantly shifts the constraints towards GR. Our framework enables the exploration of modified gravity models using the dark energy sound speed as a physically meaningful free parameter.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how varying dark energy sound speed affects cosmological observables under modified gravity; finds dynamical dark energy linked with deviations from GR at high confidence, but constraints shift towards GR when including lensing data; proposes dark energy sound speed as a key parameter for probing modified gravity.
AI.motivation: To distinguish different candidate models of dynamical dark energy through their perturbative behavior controlled by the effective sound speed, and to explore correlations between dark energy sound speed and cosmological perturbations under modified gravity scenarios.
AI.method: Testing modified gravity scenarios where dark energy equation of state and sound speed modify matter clustering; analyzing impact of varying dark energy sound speed on cosmological observables within GR and MG frameworks; constraining parameters using CMB (Planck PR4), SN (Pantheon+), BAO (DESI DR2), and cosmic shear (DES-Y3) data.
AI.result: In MG scenarios, dynamical dark energy preference correlates with deviations from GR at >95% confidence for z<2; this correlation persists with dynamical or superluminal sound speeds but disappears assuming a cosmological constant. Inclusion of cosmic shear and CMB lensing data shifts constraints towards GR.
AI.conclusion: Dark energy sound speed is a physically meaningful free parameter to explore modified gravity models, enabling distinction of underlying physics of dynamical dark energy and its perturbative signatures.

title: Decaying Dark Matter as a Possible Solution for Cosmological Tensions
summary: Large-scale structure measurements have revealed persistent tensions between early- and late-time cosmological probes, most notably the long-standing discrepancy in the structure-growth parameter $S_8$. In this work, we explore how a model including decaying dark matter (DDM) can alleviate this tension by suppressing the growth of matter fluctuations at late times. Specifically, we consider a neutrinophilic decay channel in which a heavy dark matter particle $χ$ slowly decays into a Standard Model neutrino and a light invisible fermion, $χ\rightarrow ν+ φ$, modifying both the background evolution and the clustering of structure. Using the DES Year~1 redshift distributions, we construct a baseline matter power spectrum and compute the galaxy-galaxy, shear-shear, and galaxy-shear angular power spectra under both $Λ$CDM and DDM-inspired scenarios. We find that slow dark matter decay produces a scale-dependent suppression of clustering that remains consistent with DES measurements while naturally shifting the predicted structure amplitude toward the lower values favored by weak lensing surveys. Our results suggest that decaying dark matter is a compelling and physically motivated framework for addressing the $S_8$ tension.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that a decaying dark matter model, where dark matter slowly decays into neutrinos and light fermions, can suppress matter clustering and reduce the $S_8$ tension between early- and late-time cosmological probes, fitting well with DES Year 1 data.
AI.motivation: To address the persistent tension in the cosmological structure-growth parameter $S_8$ between early- and late-time probes.
AI.method: Introducing a decaying dark matter (DDM) model with a neutrinophilic decay channel where heavy dark matter decays into a Standard Model neutrino and a light invisible fermion, and comparing predictions with DES Year 1 data via matter power spectra and angular power spectra analyses.
AI.result: The DDM model produces a scale-dependent suppression of clustering consistent with DES measurements, shifting the predicted structure amplitude towards lower values favored by weak lensing surveys, thus alleviating the $S_8$ tension.
AI.conclusion: Decaying dark matter with a neutrinophilic decay channel offers a physically motivated solution that can reconcile discrepancies in the $S_8$ parameter between early- and late-time cosmological observations.

title: On the Faint Early-time Radio and X-ray Emissions in TDE2025aarm
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, submitted to ApJL, comments welcome!!!
summary: TDE2025aarm is a nearby tidal disruption event whose early radio and X-ray emissions are exceptionally faint compared with previously observed TDEs. We examine whether these weak signals can be explained within standard outflow and disk-emission scenarios. The radio detection at $15\,\rm GHz$ with $\sim10^{36}\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}$ around $40\,\rm days$ after discovery is inconsistent with synchrotron emission from a quasi-spherical disk wind for reasonable circum-nuclear densities and outflow velocities. Instead, the low luminosity and inferred self-absorbed spectrum imply a narrowly collimated outflow with a solid angle $\lesssim0.1\,\rm sr$, naturally identified with the unbound stellar debris. The X-ray emission is likewise unusually faint, with $L_{\rm X}\sim10^{39-40}\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}$ during the first few months. If interpreted as thermal emission from an obscured accretion disk, the inferred emitting area would correspond to an implausibly small X-ray-transparent region expected to vary on short dynamical timescales that are not observed. Alternatively, the same shock responsible for the radio emission can accelerate relativistic electrons that produce X-rays through synchrotron radiation and/or inverse-Compton scattering of optical/UV photons. Both mechanisms can explain the early faint X-ray emission, although their temporal evolution differs. Continued radio and X-ray monitoring of TDE2025aarm will provide a sensitive probe of the unbound debris, circum-nuclear medium, and high-energy emission mechanisms in optical TDEs.

AI.tldr: TDE2025aarm's unusually faint early radio and X-ray emissions are inconsistent with standard disk wind and thermal disk models but fit a narrowly collimated outflow of unbound debris producing synchrotron and inverse-Compton X-rays; ongoing monitoring will clarify outflow and emission details.
AI.motivation: To understand why the early radio and X-ray emissions of the TDE2025aarm tidal disruption event are exceptionally faint compared to previous TDEs and whether these observations fit within standard emission models.
AI.method: The authors analyze multi-wavelength data, focusing on the radio detection at 15 GHz and X-ray luminosity within the first few months post-discovery. They test scenarios including synchrotron emission from disk winds versus collimated outflows of unbound debris, and thermal disk emission versus shock-accelerated relativistic electrons for X-rays.
AI.result: The faint radio emission cannot be explained by quasi-spherical disk winds but suggests a narrowly collimated outflow associated with unbound stellar debris. The faint X-rays are inconsistent with thermal emission from a small, obscured disk region, but can be explained by synchrotron or inverse-Compton processes driven by the same shock producing the radio emission. The temporal evolution of these mechanisms differs, implying further monitoring is necessary.
AI.conclusion: The weak early radio and X-ray signals of TDE2025aarm are better explained by a collimated outflow of unbound debris and shock-driven high-energy electron acceleration rather than standard disk wind or thermal disk emission scenarios. Continuous observations can unveil key properties of the outflow geometry, surrounding medium, and emission mechanisms in optical tidal disruption events.

title: Testing the cosmological principle with quasars
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, version matched the publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The inferred velocity is consistent at the 1.56 σ level with the value of 370 km/s from a purely kinematic interpretation of the CMB dipole. Based on the motion direction component analysis, we have not found any significant deviation from cosmological principle in current released quasars data. The cosmological principle posits that the universe is homogeneous and isotropic on the large scales. In history, the cosmological principle was confirmed by various cosmological observations from CMB to large scale structure. However, several new challenges to the cosmological principle were reported in recent years, particularly in radio observations from overdispersed radio source counts to quasars. Here, we firstly present studies on the peculiar velocity of large-scale anisotropy by measuring the dipole signal from the DESI DR1 catalogue with a sample of 1,176,570 quasars (0.8 < z < 3.0). Our analysis reveals the peculiar velocity of $|v| = 443.8 \pm 204.1$ km/s towards $(l, b) = (107.4^\circ \pm 86.8^\circ, 28.4^\circ \pm 45.2^\circ)$ in Galactic coordinates.The motion direction deviates from the CMB dipole (264.02$^\circ$, 48.253$^\circ$). The inferred velocity is consistent at the 1.56 $σ$ level with the value of 370 km/s from a purely kinematic interpretation of the CMB dipole. Based on the motion direction component analysis, we have not found any significant deviation from cosmological principle in current released quasars data.

AI.tldr: The paper measures large-scale velocity anisotropy from over one million quasars, finding peculiar velocity consistent with the CMB dipole within uncertainties, thereby supporting the cosmological principle without significant deviations.
AI.motivation: This paper aims to test the cosmological principle, which states that the universe is homogeneous and isotropic on large scales, given recent challenges from anisotropy detected in radio source counts and quasars.
AI.method: The study measures the dipole anisotropy signal to infer peculiar velocity by analyzing a large quasar sample (1,176,570 quasars, redshift 0.8 < z < 3.0) from the DESI DR1 catalogue, focusing on velocity magnitude and direction in Galactic coordinates.
AI.result: The inferred peculiar velocity magnitude is 443.8 ± 204.1 km/s towards (l, b) = (107.4° ± 86.8°, 28.4° ± 45.2°), deviating in direction from the CMB dipole but consistent within 1.56σ with the CMB kinematic velocity of 370 km/s.
AI.conclusion: No significant deviation from the cosmological principle is found in the current quasar data, supporting the universe's isotropy and homogeneity at large scales despite some directional deviation from the CMB dipole.

title: Far-infrared synchrotron properties of the inner lobes of the radio galaxy Centaurus A revealed with the Herschel observatory
comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, accepted for PASJ
summary: Diffuse far-infrared synchrotron emission filling the northern inner lobe of the radio galaxy Centaurus A is investigated with the Spectral and Photometric Imaging Receiver onboard the Herschel observatory at its three photometric bands. The far-infrared flux density spatially integrated over the lobe is measured as $S_{\rm ν} = 1.63 \pm 0.05$ Jy at the wavelength of $500$ $μ$m (the frequency of $600$ GHz). A comparison between the far-infrared spectral index derived with Herschel ($α= 1.32 \pm 0.19$) and the radio index ($α= 0.66 \pm 0.04$) suggests a spectral break between these frequency ranges. The change of the spectral index through the break is indicated to be consistent with that of the standard cooling break ($Δα= 0.5$) predicted for particle acceleration under the continuous energy injection condition. A broken power-law model incorporating the standard cooling break yields the break frequency as $ν_{\rm b} = 218 \pm 83$ GHz. From the measured cooling break frequency, the magnetic field of the northern inner lobe is evaluated as $B \gtrsim 100$ $μ$G. It is quantitatively estimated that the adiabatic cooling puts only a minor impact on the derived magnetic field. This magnetic field is higher than that under the minimum-energy condition by more than a factor of $5$. In addition, the derived magnetic field of the lobe is suggested to be at least by a factor of $4$ stronger than that of the inner-jet region implied in the previous very-high-energy gamma-ray study. Even if the line-of-sight orientation of the lobe is considered in its possible extreme case, the magnetic field is found to be reduced only by a factor of 2, and the above arguments about the strong magnetic field basically holds. The science impact of this result is discussed from the viewpoints of jet energetics, and of ultra-high energy cosmic rays.

AI.tldr: This study uses Herschel SPIRE data to detect a spectral break in the northern inner lobe of Centaurus A, revealing a strong magnetic field (≥100 μG) that exceeds previous estimates. The results support continuous particle acceleration and have implications for jet energetics and ultra-high energy cosmic ray origins.
AI.motivation: To investigate the diffuse far-infrared synchrotron emission in the northern inner lobe of radio galaxy Centaurus A in order to understand its magnetic field properties and particle acceleration mechanisms.
AI.method: Utilization of the Spectral and Photometric Imaging Receiver (SPIRE) onboard the Herschel observatory to measure far-infrared flux density at three photometric bands, analysis of spectral indices to identify spectral breaks, and application of a broken power-law model to estimate the cooling break frequency and magnetic field strength.
AI.result: Detection of a spectral break consistent with standard cooling break theory, determination of the break frequency at 218 ± 83 GHz, and an estimated magnetic field strength of ≥100 μG in the northern inner lobe, significantly higher than minimum-energy condition estimates and previous inner-jet region values. The magnetic field strength remains robust even under extreme line-of-sight orientation assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The northern inner lobe of Centaurus A exhibits a strong magnetic field significantly exceeding prior estimates, consistent with continuous particle acceleration and cooling processes. This finding has important implications for understanding jet energetics and the production of ultra-high energy cosmic rays in radio galaxies.

title: Calibrating Self-Weighted Shear Estimation via Field Distortion
comment: Submitted to Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics. Welcome comments!
summary: Accurate cosmic shear measurement is the key to fully realize the scientific potential of large scale galaxy surveys. The Fourier\_Quad shear measurement method has been significantly developed to avoid biases caused by various factors, including the point spread function (PSF), photon noise, pixelation effect, selection effects, etc.. Shear statistics has also been optimized by using the PDF-SYM method (symmetrization of the Probability Distribution Function of the shear estimators) to achieve the minimal statistical error, without introducing systematic error. Nevertheless, the iterative nature of the PDF-SYM method makes it computationally expensive for massive datasets. To substantially improve efficiency, we introduce the Self-Weighted Shear Estimation (SWSE) method, which employs a specific self-weighting scheme to naturally suppress the shape noise as well as to balance the contributions from the bright and faint galaxies. Because SWSE is intrinsically biased, the primary focus of this work is to robustly evaluate whether the field-distortion test (FD test, a way to calibrate the shear bias on real data) can accurately recover and correct these inherent multiplicative and additive biases. Using both simulated and real survey data, we demonstrate that the FD test can successfully calibrate SWSE on galaxy-galaxy lensing measurements, enabling it to achieve statistical precision comparable to PDF-SYM. Our results establish the combination of FD test and SWSE as a robust shear estimation approach for forthcoming large-scale weak lensing surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the Self-Weighted Shear Estimation method enhanced by the field-distortion test to efficiently and accurately measure cosmic shear, achieving performance comparable to existing methods while reducing computational cost for large datasets.
AI.motivation: To improve the efficiency of accurate cosmic shear measurements for large-scale galaxy surveys, addressing computational expense issues in existing methods.
AI.method: Introduce the Self-Weighted Shear Estimation (SWSE) method with a self-weighting scheme to suppress shape noise and balance galaxy contributions, combined with the field-distortion (FD) test for bias calibration.
AI.result: Demonstrated that the FD test can accurately calibrate the inherent biases of SWSE using both simulated and real data, enabling shear measurements with statistical precision comparable to the PDF-SYM method.
AI.conclusion: The combination of the FD test and SWSE provides a robust and efficient shear estimation approach suitable for upcoming large-scale weak lensing surveys.

title: Comparative properties of X-Ray Flashes and Gamma-Ray Bursts from BeppoSAX observations of Fast X-ray Transients
summary: We present the homogeneous and complete sample of 96 bona-fide Gamma Ray Bursts (GRBs) detected by the Wide Field Cameras and Gamma Ray Burst Monitor of BeppoSAX. We derive the spectral and temporal properties of the prompt emission, and assess the properties of the soft population of GRB, namely X-ray flashes (XRFs) in comparison with normal GRBs. We find that 36 events are XRFs, 40 X-ray rich events (XRR), and 20 normal GRBs. We analyze the distribution of the spectral parameters of the Band function, finding that the spectral indexes of the three classes are broadly similar. On the contrary the peak energy is the parameter driving the spectra shape, from 8.5 keV for XRF keV to 83 keV for GRBs. For the 67 events that are detected in both instruments we find that 9 events exhibit a soft X-ray precursor taking place from 14 to 105 s before the onset of the gamma-ray burst. About 90\% of the events that were identified in real time exhibit an X-ray afterglow, with a similar fraction for the three classes. In the optical and radio the the corresponding fractions are 35% and 33%. All the similarities in the spectrum, duration and afterglow properties suggest common progenitors for the three classes, where the differences are likely a combination of the effect of different baryon loading, energy, structure and orientation of the jet with respect to the observer. A comparison with Einstein Probe shows that the latter, thanks to its sensitivity, reaches out to a population of fainter and more numerous events, whose presence was firstly hinted at by the unique very low luminosity BeppoSAX GRB980425.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an analysis of 96 GRBs from BeppoSAX, showing that X-ray flashes, X-ray rich events, and normal GRBs share common origins despite differences in spectral peak energies, with afterglow detections supporting a unified progenitor model influenced by jet structure and observer angle.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature and distinctions among different classes of GRBs, particularly the soft population (X-ray flashes and X-ray rich events) compared to normal GRBs, and to assess their progenitor scenarios.
AI.method: The study analyzed a homogeneous and complete sample of 96 Gamma Ray Bursts detected by BeppoSAX's Wide Field Cameras and Gamma Ray Burst Monitor, deriving their spectral and temporal properties using the Band function and examining afterglow characteristics across X-ray, optical, and radio bands.
AI.result: The sample was classified into 36 XRFs, 40 XRRs, and 20 normal GRBs with similar spectral indexes but differing peak energies. A subset showed soft X-ray precursors. About 90% exhibited X-ray afterglows, while optical and radio afterglows were less common. Comparison with Einstein Probe suggests it detects fainter, more numerous GRBs previously hinted at by BeppoSAX data.
AI.conclusion: The similarities in spectral, temporal, and afterglow properties among X-ray flashes, X-ray rich events, and normal GRBs indicate they share common progenitors. Differences arise from variations in baryon loading, energy, jet structure, and observer orientation.

title: Generative Diffusion Priors for 3D Mapping of the Dark Universe
summary: Reconstructing the three-dimensional distribution of dark matter from weak-lensing observations is a central but highly ill-posed inverse problem in cosmology. Unlike standard 3D reconstruction with multiple viewpoints, we observe the universe from a single line of sight, through noisy shape distortions of galaxies with uncertain distances, so meaningful recovery of the 3D matter field requires strong prior assumptions. Existing methods either produce point estimates with handcrafted priors or use neural ensembles for approximate Bayesian uncertainty, and struggle to capture the non-Gaussian, filamentary structure of the cosmic web. With the advent of new high-resolution cosmological simulations, we now have an alternative source of prior knowledge that captures the nonlinear statistics of structure formation with far greater fidelity than analytic prescriptions. We leverage these simulations to build a new dataset $\texttt{Conicus3D}$, which enables us to learn a data-driven diffusion-model prior capturing the full 3D distribution of dark matter structure across cosmic time. Building on recent plug-and-play approaches, we modify a diffusion-based posterior sampling scheme to the 3D weak-lensing setting, combining the learned prior with a differentiable physical forward model. On realistic simulations targeting a modern weak lensing survey, our approach yields substantially improved 2D and 3D reconstruction accuracy over baseline methods. Moreover, it produces posterior samples whose statistics closely track the underlying simulations, while remaining robust to moderate shifts in cosmology.

AI.tldr: They improve 3D dark matter mapping from weak-lensing by learning a diffusion-model prior from simulations, combining it with a physical forward model to outperform existing methods in accuracy and uncertainty representation.
AI.motivation: Current methods for 3D reconstruction of dark matter from weak-lensing data struggle due to the ill-posed nature of the problem, noisy observations from a single line of sight, and difficulty capturing complex cosmic structures with handcrafted priors or approximate Bayesian neural ensembles.
AI.method: They create a new dataset (Conicus3D) from high-resolution cosmological simulations to learn a data-driven diffusion-model prior that captures the nonlinear 3D dark matter distribution. They adapt a diffusion-based posterior sampling scheme to combine this learned prior with a differentiable physical forward model for 3D weak-lensing reconstruction.
AI.result: Their approach significantly improves 2D and 3D reconstruction accuracy compared to baseline methods on realistic simulations, generates posterior samples with statistics matching underlying simulations, and maintains robustness under moderate cosmological parameter shifts.
AI.conclusion: Utilizing data-driven diffusion-model priors learned from cosmological simulations in a plug-and-play Bayesian framework greatly enhances the accuracy and reliability of 3D dark matter reconstructions from weak-lensing observations, effectively capturing cosmic web structures and posterior uncertainties.

title: BBH-Genesis: Disentangling Binary Black Hole Formation Channels with GWTC-4
summary: The detected population of binary black holes (BBHs) from the gravitational wave (GW) data has made it possible to decipher their formation and evolution history over cosmic time. The complexity of astrophysical modeling of binary mergers makes it challenging to predict key signatures for different formation channels. As a result, one of the major avenues to discover the presence of different channels from detected GW events is through a data-driven way which can isolate different scenarios. In this spirit, we developed a new inference pipeline BBH-Genesis and applied it on the fourth GW catalog (GWTC-4) to identify the presence of multiple underlying distinct populations. We find that the current population of all the binary events in GWTC-4 can be explained with the strongest evidence for only a two-channel scenario, hinting at the presence of a non-isolated binary formation channel. This sub-population can be further divided into a third channel with mild support towards formation in AGN exhibiting a slightly different effective spin and mass ratio correlation. In the future, with the detection of more events, it will be clearer whether it is necessary to consider at least three channels to explain the BBH events detected using GW observations.

AI.tldr: A new inference pipeline applied to GWTC-4 suggests that binary black hole populations are best described by two main formation channels, with tentative evidence for a third related to AGN environments.
AI.motivation: To decipher the formation and evolution history of binary black holes (BBHs) over cosmic time through gravitational wave (GW) data, despite the complexity of astrophysical modeling for binary mergers.
AI.method: Development of a new inference pipeline called BBH-Genesis and applying it to the fourth GW catalog (GWTC-4) to identify multiple distinct underlying populations of BBHs.
AI.result: Current BBH population in GWTC-4 is best explained by two formation channels, indicating a non-isolated binary formation channel. There is also mild support for a third channel possibly related to formation in AGN, characterized by slight effective spin and mass ratio differences.
AI.conclusion: The BBH events detected so far can be primarily explained by two formation channels, but future GW detections may clarify the need for at least three channels to comprehensively explain BBH populations.

title: A short review on Quintom dark energy theory
summary: In this paper, we provide a short review on the Quintom dark energy theory. Firstly, we discuss the No-Go theorem associated with dynamical dark energy, then present some examples of models in which the equation of state (EoS) evolves with time and can cross $w=-1$ . Secondly, we discuss the bouncing universe and emergent universe with Quintom matter. Finally, we discuss the possibility of studying the nature of dark energy by measuring the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) polarization rotation angle.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews Quintom dark energy theory, discussing its theoretical foundation, cosmological applications, and observational prospects via CMB polarization.
AI.motivation: To explore the Quintom dark energy theory which allows the equation of state to cross the cosmological constant boundary, addressing limitations of standard dark energy models.
AI.method: Reviewing the No-Go theorem related to dynamical dark energy, presenting models with time-evolving equation of state crossing w=-1, discussing cosmological scenarios like bouncing and emergent universes with Quintom matter, and examining the potential of CMB polarization rotation measurements.
AI.result: Identification of models that successfully realize Quintom behavior, insights on cosmological implications such as bouncing and emergent universes driven by Quintom matter, and highlighting CMB polarization rotation as a tool to probe dark energy nature.
AI.conclusion: Quintom dark energy models provide a viable framework to describe dynamic crossing of w=-1 in the equation of state, offer interesting cosmological scenarios, and can be probed through CMB polarization rotation measurements.

title: The Delta Resonance in the Neutrino Sky
summary: Recent measurements of the diffuse cosmic neutrino flux by IceCube show evidence for a spectral break at an energy near $E_ν\sim 30$ TeV. In this letter, we suggest that this feature may be due to the $Δ$-baryon resonance in $pγ$ interactions. We show that the measured spectrum, including the observed break, can be naturally accommodated by a flux of protons accelerated with a spectrum $dN_p /dE_p \propto E_p^{-3.1}$ interacting with X-rays of typical energy $E_γ \sim 0.3\,{\rm keV}$. We also point out that the presence of this spectral break significantly reduces the contribution of neutrino sources to the isotropic gamma-ray background, alleviating the longstanding tension between these measurements. In the $Δ$-resonance scenario, the gamma rays accompanying neutrino production cascade down to MeV-GeV energies and contribute at the $\sim 10\%$ level to the isotropic gamma-ray background at $\sim 3$~GeV. If our proposal is realized, it may imply that we have identified the dominant sources that produce the extragalactic cosmic rays.

AI.tldr: The IceCube neutrino spectrum break at ~30 TeV is explained by Δ-baryon resonance in proton-X-ray interactions, resolving gamma-ray background tension and pointing to dominant extragalactic cosmic ray sources.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed spectral break at ~30 TeV in the diffuse cosmic neutrino flux measured by IceCube and resolve the tension between neutrino and gamma-ray backgrounds.
AI.method: Proposed that the spectral break arises from the Δ-baryon resonance in proton-photon (pγ) interactions; modeled proton flux with a spectrum dN_p/dE_p ∝ E_p^-3.1 interacting with typical 0.3 keV X-rays; analyzed resulting neutrino and gamma-ray spectra.
AI.result: The model naturally reproduces the observed neutrino spectral break; predicts that gamma rays produced alongside neutrinos cascade to MeV-GeV energies contributing ~10% to the isotropic gamma-ray background at ~3 GeV; reduces the expected neutrino source contribution to the gamma-ray background, alleviating previous measurement tensions.
AI.conclusion: The spectral break in the cosmic neutrino flux can be explained by Δ-resonance in pγ interactions with X-rays, identifying the dominant sources of extragalactic cosmic rays and reconciling neutrino and gamma-ray observations.

title: Optimal Transport Reconstruction of Biased Tracers in Primordial Non-Gaussian Fields
summary: Optimal transport provides an efficient method to infer the displacement of objects by mapping their initial positions to their present-day locations over cosmic time; equivalently, it enables the reconstruction of initial positions from measurements taken at later times. The method has been shown to be accurate even if positions for only a biased subset of the particles are measured, provided that the initial displacement field was Gaussian. The method does not rely on the assumption of a Gaussian displacement field, and thus may be extended to the reconstruction of non-Gaussian initial conditions. Here, we demonstrate how this is achieved for a class of "local" primordial non-Gaussian fields of current interest in cosmology. For these models, there is a distinctive signature in the large scale clustering of biased tracers which depends on the product of the primordial amplitude $f_{\rm NL}$ and the nature of the tracers $b_φ$. Our method exploits the fact that this signature is not present in the full field; it is only present in biased fields. Therefore, the mass that is not in the biased subset, what we call the "dust", also has a characteristic scale-dependence, albeit of a different amplitude. We show that the quality of the optimal transport reconstruction improves as the model for this dust becomes more realistic.

AI.tldr: This paper extends optimal transport methods to reconstruct non-Gaussian initial cosmic conditions by leveraging clustering signatures of biased tracers and modeling unobserved mass, improving reconstruction quality.
AI.motivation: To extend optimal transport methods to reconstruct non-Gaussian initial conditions in cosmology, which traditional methods assuming Gaussian displacement fields cannot handle.
AI.method: Applying optimal transport reconstruction to local primordial non-Gaussian fields by exploiting the distinct scale-dependent clustering signatures of biased tracers and modeling the 'dust' (mass not in biased tracers) to improve reconstruction accuracy.
AI.result: Demonstrated improved quality of optimal transport reconstruction as the model for the 'dust' becomes more realistic; established the method's ability to handle non-Gaussian initial conditions using the distinct signatures in biased tracer clustering.
AI.conclusion: Optimal transport reconstruction methods can be successfully extended to non-Gaussian primordial fields by incorporating realistic models for the untraced mass components, enhancing the accuracy of large-scale structure reconstructions beyond Gaussian assumptions.

title: Hard X-ray Sources in Fermi UFOs
comment: 29 pages, 11 tables, 7 figures, accepted for publication on ApJ
summary: Identification and/or association of unidentified $γ$-ray sources with lower-energy counterparts represents a key challenge in modern astronomy, due to the relatively large positional uncertainty provided by $γ$-ray detectors. We selected Unidentified Fermi Objects (UFOs) positionally compatible with hard X-ray sources in the latest Palermo Swift-BAT hard X-ray Catalog and in the SRG/ART-XC all-sky X-ray survey Catalog, to identify lower-energy sources and possibly associate them to the UFOs. We found 17 UFOs with overlapping hard X-ray sources. We then collected soft X-ray data from Swift-XRT, Chandra-ACIS, XMM-Newton-EPIC, and eROSITA, identified 16 soft X-ray counterparts to the hard X-ray sources, and associate 15 with known astronomical objects, classified as: blazars/blazars candidates (2 sources), Seyfert galaxies (5 sources), X-ray binaries (2 sources), generic X-ray sources (1 source), cataclysmic variables (2 sources), and variable stars (3 sources). Blazars and Seyfert galaxies are likely lower-energy counterparts to the UFOs, since their mid-IR colors and broad-band spectral energy distributions suggest significant jetted, non-thermal emission. X-ray binaries can be potential lower-energy counterparts to the UFOs, since this class of sources has been already observed to emit $γ$-rays. The generic X-ray source has been proposed as a pulsar candidate, and we therefore suggest that it can be the lower-energy counterpart to the UFO. Cataclysmic variables have been suggested as potential $γ$-ray emitters so, if confirmed, the 2 sources classified as cataclysmic variables would represent the first $γ$-ray emitting sources of this kind. Finally, we consider the association of the 3 variable stars with the UFOs unlikely.

AI.tldr: This study cross-correlated unidentified γ-ray sources with hard and soft X-ray catalogs to identify lower-energy counterparts, associating most UFOs with known objects like blazars, Seyfert galaxies, and X-ray binaries, and proposing cataclysmic variables as potential new γ-ray sources.
AI.motivation: The study aims to address the challenge of associating unidentified γ-ray sources with lower-energy counterparts, overcoming the large positional uncertainty of γ-ray detectors.
AI.method: The authors cross-matched Unidentified Fermi Objects (UFOs) with hard X-ray sources from the Palermo Swift-BAT and SRG/ART-XC catalogs, then analyzed soft X-ray data from Swift-XRT, Chandra-ACIS, XMM-Newton-EPIC, and eROSITA to identify potential counterparts and associated them with known astronomical objects based on their characteristics.
AI.result: They identified 17 UFOs overlapping with hard X-ray sources and found 16 soft X-ray counterparts, associating 15 with known objects including blazars, Seyfert galaxies, X-ray binaries, cataclysmic variables, and variable stars. Blazars and Seyferts were considered likely counterparts due to non-thermal emission signatures; X-ray binaries and a proposed pulsar candidate were also potential counterparts. Two cataclysmic variables, if confirmed as γ-ray emitters, could represent a new class of γ-ray sources, while association with variable stars was deemed unlikely.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully identified lower-energy counterparts for most UFOs, highlighting blazars, Seyfert galaxies, X-ray binaries, and possibly pulsars as γ-ray emitters, and suggesting cataclysmic variables as a novel γ-ray source class, while ruling out variable stars as counterparts.

title: Primordial black holes spin from cosmological first-order phase transitions
summary: The stochastic bubble nucleation during cosmological first-order phase transitions leads to variations in the phase transition initiation times across different Hubble volumes, thereby generating non-Gaussian density perturbations in regions with delayed transitions. Based on the accumulation mechanism and the false vacuum island model . This paper investigates the spin angular momentum of primordial black holes formed from nonspherical collapse. By introducing the nucleation history integration method, without assuming a Gaussian distribution, we calculate the expectation values and variances of the semi-axis lengths of overdense ellipsoidal regions, combined with the statistical properties of the velocity shear tensor, we derive the quantitative relationship between the Kerr parameter $a_*$ describing black hole spin and the phase transition parameters , latent heat strength $α$ and phase transition rate $β$. The study finds that the Kerr parameter increases with $α$ and decreases with $β$; estimate the typical the magnitude of $a_*$ can reach $10^{-3}$, which is significantly higher than that of primordial black holes formed in the radiation-dominated era under peak theory, but still lower than that in a matter-dominated era.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the spin of primordial black holes formed from nonspherical collapse during stochastic bubble nucleation in first-order cosmological phase transitions, introducing a nucleation history integration method to link black hole spin (Kerr parameter) with phase transition parameters, finding spins around $10^{-3}$ influenced by latent heat and transition rate.
AI.motivation: To investigate the spin angular momentum of primordial black holes formed from nonspherical collapse during stochastic bubble nucleation in cosmological first-order phase transitions, addressing the generation of non-Gaussian density perturbations due to variations in phase transition initiation times across Hubble volumes.
AI.method: The paper introduces the nucleation history integration method to calculate expectation values and variances of semi-axis lengths of overdense ellipsoidal regions without assuming Gaussian distributions. It combines these results with the statistical properties of the velocity shear tensor to derive quantitative relations between the Kerr parameter and phase transition parameters.
AI.result: The study quantitatively relates the Kerr parameter to phase transition parameters, finding it increases with latent heat strength and decreases with phase transition rate, estimating typical spin values around $10^{-3}$, higher than those from radiation-era peak theory but less than matter-era cases.
AI.conclusion: The Kerr parameter of primordial black holes formed during first-order cosmological phase transitions is found to increase with latent heat strength $α$ and decrease with the phase transition rate $β$, with typical magnitudes around $10^{-3}$. This spin magnitude is notably higher than that of primordial black holes formed via peak theory in the radiation-dominated era but lower than those formed in a matter-dominated era.

title: Suppression of boosted relic neutrinos by photon backgrounds during ultra-high-energy cosmic ray propagation
summary: Constraining the cosmic neutrino background (C$ν$B) represents a major experimental challenge in cosmology. Recent studies have suggested that relic neutrinos boosted by ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) may generate observable diffuse neutrino fluxes. Previous estimates have not effectively propagated the primary cosmic rays, often neglecting crucial energy losses and the unavoidable, competing interactions with diffuse photon backgrounds. Here we revisit these expectations using a realistic Monte Carlo propagation framework. This approach allows us to consistently incorporate cosmic ray energy losses, nuclear photodisintegration, and production of secondary neutrinos. We show that interactions with diffuse photon backgrounds strongly suppress the boosted relic neutrino flux predicted in simplified propagation scenarios. Furthermore, we demonstrate that to produce any observable suppression on the UHECR energy spectrum at Earth, or for the boosted C$ν$B component to become comparable to the cosmogenic neutrino flux, the C$ν$B density must be enhanced by a factor, the so-called overdensity, of extreme magnitude ($η\gtrsim 10^{8}$).

AI.tldr: Using a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of ultra-high-energy cosmic ray propagation, the study finds that realistic energy losses and photon interactions drastically weaken the boosted cosmic neutrino background flux, requiring an unfeasibly large relic neutrino overdensity for observable effects.
AI.motivation: Previous estimates predicting observable diffuse neutrino fluxes from boosted relic neutrinos did not fully account for the propagation effects and energy losses of primary cosmic rays, potentially overestimating the flux and its observability.
AI.method: The study employs a realistic Monte Carlo propagation framework to simulate the interactions and energy losses of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, including nuclear photodisintegration and secondary neutrino production, fully propagating the cosmic rays through diffuse photon backgrounds.
AI.result: Interactions with diffuse photon backgrounds significantly reduce the boosted relic neutrino flux. For any observable suppression of the UHECR spectrum or boosted C$\nu$B flux comparable to cosmogenic neutrinos, an extreme overdensity factor ($\eta \gtrsim 10^{8}$) of relic neutrinos is necessary.
AI.conclusion: The boosted cosmic neutrino background flux is strongly suppressed when realistic cosmic ray propagation effects, including energy losses and interactions with diffuse photon backgrounds, are taken into account. Observable effects require an unrealistically high density overdensity of relic neutrinos.

title: CSST large-scale structure analysis pipeline: IV. Cosmic Voids Identified from Galaxy Group Samples as Probes of the Large-scale Structure
summary: Because groups are directly associated with halos, they allow for considerably simpler theoretical modeling than approaches based on individual galaxies. We therefore propose to use voids identified in galaxy group catalogs, referred to as group-voids, to investigate the cosmic large-scale structure (LSS). Using the reference mock galaxy redshift survey (MGRS) designed for the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST), we build two galaxy group catalogs representing ideal and conservative scenarios, derived from galaxy samples with 100\% and roughly 30\% spectroscopic redshift completeness, respectively. We then identify voids in these two mock group catalogs, as well as in the underlying halo catalog, and measure two void statistics, the void size function (VSF) and the void density profile, within five redshift intervals spanning $z=0$ to $1.0$. We compare the statistics obtained from two kinds of voids: those defined by galaxy groups (group-voids) and those defined by dark matter halos (halo-voids). In the void-finding process, we adopt the brightest central galaxy (BCG) as the group center to improve the accuracy of the inferred void centers. Our analysis shows that void statistics derived from group-voids with spectroscopic redshift completeness of at least 40\% can faithfully reproduce the corresponding statistics from halo-voids. Even when the redshift completeness of galaxies falls to as low as 30\%, we can still reliably describe group-voids via halo-voids by incorporating a redshift error term. This indicates that group-voids are a promising tool for probing LSS and offer a valuable complement to standard void studies, which is especially advantageous for emulator-based methods.

AI.tldr: This study demonstrates that voids identified in galaxy group catalogs accurately represent cosmic large-scale structure voids, enabling simpler modeling and effective analysis even with moderate spectroscopic completeness.
AI.motivation: To simplify theoretical modeling of cosmic large-scale structure by using galaxy groups rather than individual galaxies for void identification.
AI.method: Constructed galaxy group catalogs from mock galaxy redshift surveys with varying spectroscopic redshift completeness; identified voids in these catalogs and in halo catalogs; measured void size function and void density profile across multiple redshift slices; compared void statistics between group-voids and halo-voids using brightest central galaxy as group center.
AI.result: Void statistics from group-voids with ≥40% spectroscopic completeness closely match those from halo-voids; even at 30% completeness, reliable void descriptions are achieved by accounting for redshift errors.
AI.conclusion: Group-voids identified from galaxy group catalogs are effective and reliable probes of large-scale structure, providing a simpler and complementary approach to standard void studies, especially useful for emulator-based methodologies.

title: The Radio--X-ray Correlation of High-Redshift AGN: A Numerical Study of Inverse-Compton Scattering of the CMB Photons in Relativistic Jets
summary: Relativistic jets from active galactic nuclei are expected to exhibit strong redshift evolution in their radiative output due to the increasing energy density of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We investigate the role of inverse Compton (IC) scattering of CMB photons in regulating the radio and X-ray emission from large-scale jets using three-dimensional relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations coupled with a hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian particle framework. By keeping the jet dynamics and ambient medium properties fixed across redshifts, we are able to isolate the impact of the cosmological evolution of the CMB on the jet radiation. From our simulations, we construct synthetic spectral energy distributions and intensity maps considering synchrotron and IC/CMB losses along with particle acceleration from shocks. We are able to reproduce the weak redshift dependence of radio luminosity and the strong enhancement of X-ray emission toward high redshift that is observed in radio-loud quasars. At high redshift, the X-ray luminosity follows the expected $(1+z)^4$ scaling, confirming IC/CMB as the dominant mechanism driving the X-ray enhancement. The resulting X-ray-to-radio flux ratio increases systematically with redshift and is consistent with observational constraints. Finally, we show that slower jets exhibit a stronger redshift evolution of the X-ray enhancement than faster jets, highlighting the critical role of jet propagation length scales and particle energy evolution. The simulations also naturally reproduce the steepening of the radio spectral index with redshift - the $α$-$z$ relation - thus providing a unified framework that allows to interpret the multiwavelength properties of high-redshift radio sources.

AI.tldr: This study uses 3D relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations to show that the increase in CMB energy density with redshift drives stronger X-ray emission in AGN jets via inverse Compton scattering, explaining observed multiwavelength properties and their evolution with redshift.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of the cosmological evolution of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) on the radiative output of relativistic jets from active galactic nuclei, particularly their radio and X-ray emission, across different redshifts.
AI.method: Utilizing three-dimensional relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations combined with a hybrid Eulerian-Lagrangian particle framework to model jet dynamics and particle acceleration, while isolating the effect of CMB energy density increase with redshift on jet radiation. Synthetic spectral energy distributions and intensity maps were generated, considering synchrotron and inverse Compton (IC) scattering losses.
AI.result: The simulations reproduce the observed weak redshift dependence of radio luminosity and a strong X-ray luminosity enhancement at high redshift that follows the $(1+z)^4$ scaling, confirming IC/CMB scattering as the dominant mechanism. The X-ray-to-radio flux ratio increases with redshift, consistent with observational data. Slower jets show a stronger redshift evolution in X-ray emission. The model also explains the steepening of the radio spectral index with redshift ($α$-$z$ relation).
AI.conclusion: Inverse Compton scattering of CMB photons is the primary driver of redshift evolution in X-ray emission from relativistic jets, producing observationally consistent multiwavelength features of high-redshift radio sources. Jet speed significantly influences the degree of X-ray enhancement with redshift, and the simulations provide a comprehensive framework to interpret these phenomena.

title: Redshift Duality with Pantheon+SH0ES in a Planck-anchored Flat $Λ$CDM Framework: Implications for Hubble Tension and Observational Inference
comment: Author version comprising 31 pages and 5 figures. Compiled in the MNRAS LaTeX style. Compared with the Advance Access version, this version includes accessibility-related updates to figure captions, updated affiliation and acknowledgements, revised citation labels, and corrected mathematical notation
summary: We test an operationally defined redshift duality in which the observed redshift comprises the standard metric-expansion component together with an additional line-of-sight quantum contribution arising from the cumulative conversion of photon energy into effective mass as a function of path length and frequency. Fitting this hybrid model to the Pantheon+SH0ES compilation, we find that the metric-expansion Hubble constant, $H_Λ$, is recovered to a value consistent with the Planck baseline of $67.4~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ within $\lesssim 0.33σ$. Redshift-binned analyses show that while the flat Lambda cold dark matter ($Λ$CDM) model produces an apparent drift in the inferred Hubble parameter across the Hubble flow, the hybrid model restores the constancy of $H_Λ$ across redshift bins. The correctional trends of cosmological physical quantities re-inferred under this framework further indicate the potential to alleviate anomalies associated with high-redshift galaxies. These results suggest that redshift duality warrants further consideration in observational processing and inference, while preserving consistency with a Planck-anchored flat $Λ$CDM baseline.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid redshift model adding a quantum contribution to standard cosmological redshift, fitting this model to observational data. It recovers Planck-consistent Hubble constant values and stabilizes redshift-dependent measurements, offering improved consistency and addressing certain high-redshift anomalies.
AI.motivation: To investigate an operationally defined redshift duality incorporating both the standard metric-expansion redshift and a quantum contribution from photon energy conversion, aiming to address discrepancies in cosmological measurements.
AI.method: The authors introduce a hybrid redshift model combining metric-expansion redshift with a line-of-sight quantum effect. They fit this model to the Pantheon+SH0ES supernova compilation and perform redshift-binned analyses to compare results with the standard flat ΛCDM model.
AI.result: The hybrid model recovers the Hubble constant ($H_Λ$) consistent with the Planck value within 0.33σ and removes the apparent drift in inferred Hubble parameters across redshift bins seen in the standard model. It also suggests improvements in resolving anomalies related to high-redshift galaxies.
AI.conclusion: Redshift duality incorporating quantum contributions alongside metric expansion provides a consistent cosmological framework that aligns with Planck baseline parameters, restores redshift stability in the Hubble parameter, and potentially alleviates anomalies, warranting its further consideration in cosmological data analysis.

authors: Elisabete M. de Gouveia Dal Pino
title: TeV gamma-ray spectral spikes produced by magnetic reconnection in blazar jets: the case of the 2014 high state of Markarian 501
summary: Multi-wavelength monitoring of the flaring blazar Markarian 501 during July 2014 revealed a TeV gamma-ray spike feature with 3-4$σ$ significance and coincident with a prominent enhancement in its X-ray flux. The appearance of this spectral feature strongly suggests the presence of an extra emission component in addition to the usual one-zone SSC scenario. Several possible explanations for the origin of this novel behavior have been discussed, including stochastic particle acceleration, magnetospheric vacuum gap, and pion decay. In this paper, we show that the TeV narrow feature, simultaneous with an increase in the X-ray flux, can be produced with two leptonic emission regions in a jet undergoing magnetic reconnection energy dissipation along its propagation axis. In this scenario, the stable spectral components are produced in the region of maximum magnetic dissipation. A second region produces a flare upstream in the jet in a slower, more magnetized, and much smaller region compared to the stable one, which is responsible for increasing the X-ray flux and producing the TeV spike. The macroscopic properties of these two emission regions are consistent with a magnetically striped jet model discussed in previous works, where the acceleration of the jet flow and its non-thermal emission is driven by turbulent-induced magnetic reconnection. We employ this jet-reconnection scenario to model the 2014 high state of the blazar Markarian 501, considering the sequence of SED datasets corresponding to MJD 56855.91, 56857.98, 56858.98, and 56859.97, with the second dataset being the one that exhibits the TeV spike.

AI.tldr: This paper models the 2014 high state of blazar Markarian 501, explaining a TeV gamma-ray spike and X-ray flux increase via two distinct leptonic emission zones in a jet powered by magnetic reconnection, consistent with a magnetically striped jet framework.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of a novel TeV gamma-ray spike feature coincident with an X-ray flux enhancement in the blazar Markarian 501, which cannot be explained by the usual one-zone SSC model.
AI.method: Model the blazar emission using two leptonic regions in a jet undergoing magnetic reconnection, where one region produces stable emissions and the other a flare caused by a smaller, more magnetized emission zone upstream in the jet.
AI.result: The TeV narrow feature and X-ray flux increase are successfully explained by the proposed two-region leptonic emission model driven by turbulent magnetic reconnection in a magnetically striped jet, consistent with previous jet acceleration and emission theories.
AI.conclusion: The observed TeV gamma-ray spike and X-ray enhancement in Markarian 501 during July 2014 can be accounted for by a jet-reconnection scenario involving two spatially and physically distinct emission regions, supporting the magnetically striped jet model as an effective framework for interpreting blazar high-state emission features.

title: JWST's Little Red Dots as collapsed Supermassive Dark Stars
summary: The nature of the ``Little Red Dots'' (LRDs) is one of the most profound mysteries posed by the JWST data. One promising class of models that can reproduce the observed LRDs spectra and morphology are quasi-stars: massive envelopes surrounding accreting black holes formed via the collapse of supermassive stars (SMSs). However, the canonical SMS pathway relies on a highly restricted set of environmental and structural conditions: strong Lyman--Werner (LW) backgrounds to suppress H$_2$ cooling, high and sustained gas inflow rates to enforce entropy stratified envelopes, and assume non-zero rotational support in order to prevent GR instability collapse before $\sim 10^6 M_{\odot}$. Here we show that supermassive dark stars (SMDSs), powered by dark matter (DM) annihilation rather than nuclear burning, naturally satisfy the key structural and energetic requirements for quasi-star (QS) formation while relaxing {\it all} of those restrictive conditions listed above. Moreover, quasi-stars formed through the SMDS pathway are born with prompt BH masses ($\gtrsim 10\%$) of the progenitor mass. They therefore enter directly into a late-stage quasi-star regime; subsequently the envelope expands and cools until its photosphere reaches the zero-metallicity opacity limit $(T_{\rm eff}\sim3000$-$6000\,{\rm K}$). Those cool, optically thick, unresolved photospheres can reproduce key features of many JWST LRDs.

AI.tldr: This paper suggests that supermassive dark stars can form quasi-stars without stringent environmental conditions, producing black holes and photospheres that explain the observed JWST Little Red Dots.
AI.motivation: Understanding the nature of the JWST-observed Little Red Dots (LRDs), which present significant astrophysical mysteries.
AI.method: Propose that supermassive dark stars (SMDSs), powered by dark matter annihilation, satisfy the structural and energetic conditions for quasi-star (QS) formation without the restrictive environmental requirements of the canonical supermassive star (SMS) pathway.
AI.result: SMDSs form quasi-stars with prompt black hole masses over 10% of progenitor mass, entering directly into a late-stage quasi-star phase with cool, optically thick photospheres that match key observational features of JWST LRDs.
AI.conclusion: SMDS-driven quasi-star formation relaxes previous environmental constraints and provides a natural explanation for the spectral and morphological properties of JWST LRDs.

title: High-Synchrotron-Peaked BL Lacs as Multi-Messenger Sources: Connecting Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays and Neutrinos
summary: High-synchrotron-peaked (HSP) BL Lac objects are extreme particle accelerators whose synchrotron emission peaks at high frequencies, typically in the UV-to-X-ray band ($ν_{\rm peak} > 10^{15}$ Hz; $ν_{\rm peak} \geq 10^{17}$ for EHSPs), implying electron Lorentz factors of order $10^5-10^6$. Their relative proximity ($z \geq 0.5$), clean radiation environments, and favorable Hillas parameters make them prime candidates for ultra-high-energy cosmic ray (UHECR) acceleration beyond $10^{19}$ eV and for neutrino production above 100 TeV. The 2017 association of IceCube-170922A with the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 provided compelling evidence for blazars as neutrino sources, while an archival neutrino flare from 2014-2015 with no clear electromagnetic counterpart (13 events) revealed additional complexity in the emission mechanism. This review examines HSP physical properties, identifies them through WISE-based infrared selection (the 2WHSP and 3HSP catalogs, approximately 2000 sources), and contrasts leptonic synchrotron self-Compton models with hadronic alternatives. We assess the observational evidence linking HSPs to high-energy neutrinos and UHECRs, finding that extreme baryonic loading ($L_p/L_e \sim 10^3-10^5$) strains energetic budgets, Auger composition measurements favor heavy nuclei over proton-dominated scenarios, and the near-isotropy of UHECR arrival directions is difficult to reconcile with rare beamed sources. Potential resolutions involving magnetic reconnection, structured jets, and duty cycle effects are discussed. Next-generation facilities, including IceCube-Gen2, KM3NeT, CTAO, IXPE, and AugerPrime/TA x 4, will probe key observables to either establish HSP BL Lacs as sources of the highest-energy cosmic particles or redirect the search toward alternative accelerator classes.

AI.tldr: This review evaluates high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lac objects as ultra-high-energy cosmic ray and neutrino sources, highlighting their potential and current challenges, and outlining future experimental prospects to resolve their role in high-energy astrophysics.
AI.motivation: To investigate the role of high-synchrotron-peaked (HSP) BL Lac objects as potential sources of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and high-energy neutrinos, motivated by recent observational associations (e.g., IceCube-170922A with TXS 0506+056) and complex emission mechanisms.
AI.method: Review of HSP BL Lac physical properties, infrared-based source identification via WISE catalogs (2WHSP and 3HSP), comparison of leptonic synchrotron self-Compton and hadronic emission models, and assessment of multimessenger observational data including neutrinos and cosmic rays.
AI.result: Findings indicate that while HSPs demonstrate promising characteristics for UHECR and neutrino production, constraints arise due to required extreme baryonic loading, heavy-nuclei composition favored by Auger data, and isotropy challenges of UHECR arrival directions concerning rare beamed sources. Proposed solutions involve magnetic reconnection, structured jets, and duty cycle considerations.
AI.conclusion: Although HSP BL Lacs are strong candidate sources for the highest-energy cosmic particles, current observational and theoretical challenges leave their definitive role uncertain. Upcoming advanced experimental facilities will critically test these hypotheses or necessitate alternative source classes.

title: Enhancing the Angular Resolution of Large Array of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (LACT) at Ultra-High Energies
summary: The Large Array of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (LACT) is dedicated to high-resolution morphological studies of PeVatrons. In this work, we present a fundamental investigation into stereoscopic direction reconstruction for the LACT array, specifically addressing the challenges of ultra-high-energy observations. We demonstrate that the standard Hillas parameterization introduces a significant reconstruction bias under severe image leakage. To mitigate this, we introduce an approach utilizing a 2D Gaussian fit, achieving an exceptional angular resolution of better than $0.06^\circ$ at $100\text{ TeV}$ within the central $0^\circ\text{--}1^\circ$ offset bin, and maintaining better than $0.12^\circ$ across offsets up to $4^{\circ}$. Building on this robust baseline, we evaluate advanced weighting schemes by utilizing a LightGBM-based quantile regression model to independently estimate single-image quality. Applying these quality-based weights yields a consistent improvement of $0.02^\circ$ to $0.03^\circ$ for high-energy, large-offset events using both the \textit{HillasWeightedSum} and \textit{HillasWeightedDisp} methods. Finally, to establish a theoretical performance ceiling, we explore a pixel-wise likelihood reconstruction technique utilizing Neural Ratio Estimation. While its practical realization depends heavily on minimizing the gap between Monte Carlo simulations and observational data, this exploratory approach demonstrates the potential to yield an overall improvement of approximately 15\% to 40\% at $100~\rm TeV$ across the entire field of view. Such high angular resolution is critical for disentangling complex emission regions and mapping the internal structures of PeVatrons.

AI.tldr: This paper improves ultra-high-energy direction reconstruction in LACT by replacing Hillas parameterization with a 2D Gaussian fit, enhancing resolution through LightGBM-based weighting, and proposing a neural likelihood method that could yield up to 40% better angular accuracy at 100 TeV.
AI.motivation: To improve stereoscopic direction reconstruction for ultra-high-energy observations with the Large Array of Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (LACT), addressing biases in standard methods under severe image leakage.
AI.method: Introduced a 2D Gaussian fit approach to reduce reconstruction bias, evaluated advanced weighting schemes via a LightGBM-based quantile regression model to estimate single-image quality, and explored pixel-wise likelihood reconstruction using Neural Ratio Estimation.
AI.result: Achieved angular resolution better than 0.06° at 100 TeV near the center and better than 0.12° up to 4° offset; quality-based weighting improved resolution by 0.02°–0.03° for high-energy, large-offset events; Neural Ratio Estimation indicated potential for 15%–40% overall improvement at 100 TeV across the field of view.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methods significantly enhance angular resolution for LACT, crucial for detailed morphological studies of PeVatrons, with the Neural Ratio Estimation approach offering a promising direction despite practical challenges.

title: Reconnection-Driven Injection and Stochastic Reacceleration during Cosmological Magnetogenesis
summary: We investigate whether magnetic reconnection can provide suprathermal proton seed particles during cosmological magnetogenesis prior to nonlinear structure formation. Previous work showed that pressure-anisotropy-driven stochastic acceleration alone is strongly limited by cosmological expansion and Coulomb cooling. Here, we extend this framework by adding a phenomenological reconnection-driven source term to the Fokker--Planck equation for the isotropic ion distribution, with the injection power tied to the magnetic-energy growth rate during magnetogenesis. We find that reconnection can act as a fast injection channel and can produce a visible suprathermal tail. However, the resulting nonthermal energy fraction remains very small, of order $10^{-7}$ in the fiducial model, implying a negligible nonthermal pressure contribution to the pre-structure intergalactic medium. This limitation arises because the extremely high-beta plasma contains only a small magnetic-energy reservoir, even when reconnection itself is locally fast. Using a test-particle shock reacceleration estimate, we further show that the reconnection-produced tail can enhance the suprathermal proton population available for later structure-formation shocks by about an order of magnitude. Nevertheless, the associated hadronic gamma-ray emission from low-density cluster outskirts is expected to remain far below current detectability. We therefore conclude that reconnection during cosmological magnetogenesis is unlikely to dominate the cosmic-ray energy budget directly, but may provide a low-level seed population for subsequent shock acceleration.

AI.tldr: Magnetic reconnection before structure formation can create suprathermal protons but only at negligible energy levels, insufficient for significant cosmic-ray generation or gamma-ray detection; however, it may modestly boost seed protons for later shock acceleration.
AI.motivation: To explore whether magnetic reconnection can generate suprathermal proton seed particles during cosmological magnetogenesis before nonlinear structure formation, addressing limitations of previous acceleration models.
AI.method: Extended the Fokker--Planck equation for isotropic ion distributions by including a phenomenological reconnection-driven source term linked to magnetic-energy growth, combined with a test-particle shock reacceleration estimate.
AI.result: Magnetic reconnection produces a visible suprathermal proton tail but with a very small nonthermal energy fraction (~10^-7), hence negligible impact on nonthermal pressure in the intergalactic medium. The reconnection tail can increase suprathermal protons for later shock acceleration by about an order of magnitude, but related gamma-ray signals remain undetectable.
AI.conclusion: Reconnection-driven proton acceleration during cosmological magnetogenesis is insufficient to directly impact the cosmic-ray energy budget or generate observable gamma-ray emission, though it may provide a minor seed population for subsequent shock acceleration processes.

title: Hunting for Compact Object Binaries from eRASS1 Optical Counterparts through ZTF Time-domain Photometry and Multi-wavelength Census
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, to be submitted
summary: Capitalizing on the eRASS1 optical counterpart catalog, we conduct a systematic census of compact object binary (COB) candidates, with a primary focus on X-ray binaries (XRBs), by integrating ZTF time-domain photometry with multi-wavelength observations. This framework establishes two complementary pipelines, yielding two distinct source samples. The first sample consists of 151 periodically variable sources, from which a highly refined subset of 43 high-priority COB candidates is identified. The second sample comprises 1958 distance-constrained sources selected based on elevated X-ray luminosities or high $\log (F_{\mathrm{X}}/F_{\mathrm{opt}})$. Crucially, cross-matching both samples with radio catalogs reveals seven radio-emitting sources, highlighting four promising XRB candidates. Our results underscore that coupling eROSITA with wide-field time-domain photometric and multi-wavelength surveys offers a highly efficient strategy for uncovering the hidden population of COBs.

AI.tldr: Using eRASS1 optical data combined with ZTF photometry and multi-wavelength observations, this study identifies new compact object binary candidates, demonstrating the efficiency of multi-survey integration in uncovering hidden X-ray binaries.
AI.motivation: To systematically identify and characterize compact object binary candidates, particularly X-ray binaries, by leveraging multi-wavelength data including optical, X-ray, and radio observations.
AI.method: Integration of eRASS1 optical counterpart catalog with ZTF time-domain photometry and multi-wavelength data, establishing two pipelines: one identifying periodically variable sources and another selecting distance-constrained sources based on high X-ray luminosity or flux ratios, followed by cross-matching with radio catalogs.
AI.result: Identification of 151 periodically variable sources with 43 high-priority COB candidates, and 1958 distance-constrained sources, among which seven radio-emitting sources were found, including four promising XRB candidates.
AI.conclusion: Combining eROSITA X-ray data with wide-field time-domain photometry and multi-wavelength surveys is an effective approach to discover and characterize the hidden population of compact object binaries, especially X-ray binaries.

title: Mass and Spin Growth of Very Massive Stars in Star Clusters Potentially Associated with Little Red Dots
summary: Using gravitational $N$-body simulations, we investigate the evolution of mass and spin for very massive stars (VMSs) in dense star clusters, which may be potentially associated with Little Red Dots (LRDs). Our results show that VMS masses can reach $10^3$--$10^4\,M_\odot$, depending on the initial conditions of the host clusters. Notably, the VMS mass increases by up to a factor of three when accounting for the bloated state at the Hayashi track induced by stellar collisions, provided that this state is maintained at accretion rates exceeding $3 \times 10^{-2}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. In all cases, the spin of the VMS, when normalized to the dimensionless black hole (BH) spin parameter, exceeds $10$. While our model may overestimate VMS masses and spins due to the omission of post-main-sequence evolution and the loss of mass and angular momentum during collisions, we nonetheless demonstrate that VMSs formed in dense star clusters can be highly spinning. Such a rapidly spinning VMS is expected to collapse into an intermediate-mass BH surrounded by a massive accretion disk. This BH-disk system could trigger powerful explosions and emit burst gravitational waves, similar to those observed in GW190521 and GW231123, for which the remnant BH masses are estimated to be $\gtrsim 100\,M_\odot$.
