AI.tldr: Using N-body simulations, the study shows very massive stars in dense clusters can become extremely massive and rapidly spinning, collapsing into intermediate-mass black holes that may explain certain observed gravitational wave events.
AI.motivation: To understand the evolution of mass and spin of very massive stars (VMSs) in dense star clusters and their potential connection to observed astrophysical phenomena such as Little Red Dots and gravitational wave events.
AI.method: Conduct gravitational N-body simulations modeling VMS formation and evolution within dense star clusters, accounting for stellar collisions, accretion rates, and spin parameters.
AI.result: VMS masses can reach 10^3 to 10^4 solar masses, potentially increasing by up to a factor of three under certain conditions related to the Hayashi track and high accretion rates. The normalized spin of the VMS exceeds 10, indicating very rapid rotation. These findings imply that such VMSs can form rapidly spinning intermediate-mass black holes with massive accretion disks, which may produce powerful explosive events and gravitational wave bursts similar to recent detections.
AI.conclusion: Very massive stars formed in dense star clusters can grow to extremely high masses and spins, leading to the formation of rapidly spinning intermediate-mass black holes. These black holes, surrounded by massive accretion disks, could be responsible for energetic astrophysical phenomena including gravitational wave bursts akin to GW190521 and GW231123.

title: Photon Escape from Slab Thomson Media: A Scattering-order-resolved Recursive Formalism for Comptonization Applications
summary: The scattering history of photons in slab media plays an important role in modelling Comptonized spectra and disc-corona radiative feedback. We develop a recursive formalism that evolves the post-scattering depth--direction distribution in slab Thomson media and yields boundary- and angle-resolved escape probabilities at each scattering order. For azimuth-integrated problems, the angular dependence closes within a two-component basis, reducing the transport problem to an efficient depth-kernel recursion. We apply the method to normally incident beam injection, Lambert-law boundary injection, and a vertically uniform isotropic internal source, and verify the results with Monte Carlo radiative-transfer simulations. The resulting distributions provide a photon-number-conserving route to semi-analytic Comptonized spectra and estimates of the Compton amplification factor and the fraction of downwardly scattered luminosity. We also derive the mean scattering number within this framework, obtaining the exact result $\langle N\rangle=2τ$ for Lambert-law injection, while the uniform internal source changes from an optically thin $τ\ln(1/τ)$ behaviour to an optically thick $τ^2/4$ scaling. At high scattering orders, the recursion is controlled by a dominant eigenmode: $P_n/P_{n-1}\rightarrowλ(τ)$, where $λ(τ)$ is the spectral radius of the slab recursion operator. This eigenmode also determines a limiting normalized angular distribution, so that viewing angle and escape boundary primarily affect the normalization of the high-order X-ray component, while spectral-shape differences are mainly confined to the unscattered and low-order components. These eigenvalue and eigenfunction results provide transport ingredients for future energy-dependent slab Comptonization models.

AI.tldr: Developed a recursive method to model photon scattering in slab media yielding angle- and boundary-resolved escape probabilities, validated by Monte Carlo simulations, providing an efficient framework for semi-analytic Comptonized spectra and key scattering metrics.
AI.motivation: To model Comptonized spectra and disc-corona radiative feedback more accurately by understanding the scattering history of photons in slab media.
AI.method: A recursive formalism evolving the post-scattering depth–direction distribution in slab Thomson media, closed in a two-component basis for azimuth-integrated problems, reducing transport to an efficient depth-kernel recursion; verified with Monte Carlo radiative-transfer simulations.
AI.result: Obtained boundary- and angle-resolved escape probabilities at each scattering order, photon-number-conserving Comptonized spectra, estimates of the Compton amplification factor, fraction of downward luminosity, exact mean scattering numbers for different source injections, and identified a dominant eigenmode controlling high scattering order behavior and angular distributions.
AI.conclusion: The recursive scattering formalism provides an efficient, semi-analytic approach to model Comptonized spectra in slab media with precise angular and boundary resolution, enabling improved understanding and prediction of radiative transfer and feedback in astrophysical environments, with potential for integration into future energy-dependent Comptonization models.

title: The First Detection of Sub-Populations in the Delay-Time Distribution of Binary Black Holes in GWTC-4 of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures and 1 appendix. Comments are welcome!
summary: The imprint of different formation channels of binary black holes (BBHs) is encoded in the distribution of time delays between BBH mergers and the formation of their progenitor stars, along with their source properties such as component mass, mass-ratio, spin, and more. This makes it possible for the presence of a potential correlation between the delay-time distribution and compact-object source properties. We report the first measurement of this inevitable signature from the fourth gravitational wave (GW) catalog (GWTC-4) of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA and identified three sub-populations that show distinct merger rate behavior as a consequence of this. We find that the delay-time distribution of the sources above a mass of $45$ M$_\odot$ is significantly different from the ones below and exhibits strong dependence on the mass-ratio and spin, indicating that GW sources close to equal masses and close to zero effective spin are more delayed in comparison to the values otherwise. Our analysis identifies the presence of at least three source property dependent sub-population of merger rates with the merger rate at redshift $z=0$ varying from $\sim 0.6- 12$ Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$ for the three different sub-populations and hence rule out a Universal merger rate for all the BBHs detected using GW.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first measurement of the correlation between BBH merger delay-time distributions and source properties using GWTC-4 data, identifies three distinct BBH sub-populations with varying merger rates, and rules out a universal merger rate for all detected BBHs.
AI.motivation: To investigate the correlation between the delay-time distribution of binary black hole (BBH) mergers and their source properties, which encodes information about their formation channels.
AI.method: Analyzed data from the fourth gravitational wave catalog (GWTC-4) of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA to measure the delay-time distribution and its dependence on source properties such as mass, mass-ratio, and spin.
AI.result: Identified three distinct sub-populations of BBH mergers with different merger rate behaviors and delay-time distributions, particularly distinguishing sources above and below 45 solar masses, with merger rates at redshift z=0 varying significantly across sub-populations.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals the presence of source property dependent sub-populations of BBH merger rates and rejects the hypothesis of a universal merger rate for all BBHs detected via gravitational waves.

title: Deep Optical Follow-up Observations to IceCube Cosmic Neutrinos: a case for IC230724A with Subaru/HSC and prospects with Rubin/LSST
summary: IceCube has been detecting cosmic high-energy neutrinos for more than 10 years, but their major sources are still under debate. To identify them, IceCube is issuing neutrino alerts, which enable us to perform electromagnetic follow-up observations. In this paper, we present our Subaru/HSC deep optical follow-up observations down to 25.5 mag to a well-localized neutrino event, IceCube 230724A. We conduct a dedicated analysis with extensive evaluation of background rates and true positive rates adopting the blind analysis policy to identify or disfavor tidal disruption events (TDEs) as cosmic neutrino sources. Our analysis found no TDE candidate in the region of interest. Rubin/LSST survey will enable us to constrain their fractional contribution to the cosmic high-energy neutrino background, either $\lesssim 60\%$ or $\gtrsim30\%$ for non-detection and detection, respectively, if Rubin covers the error regions of 10 neutrino events.

AI.tldr: Deep optical follow-up of IceCube neutrino event 230724A found no tidal disruption events, suggesting TDEs are unlikely sources there; upcoming surveys like Rubin/LSST will better constrain TDE contributions to cosmic high-energy neutrinos.
AI.motivation: To identify the major sources of cosmic high-energy neutrinos detected by IceCube, which remain uncertain.
AI.method: IceCube issues neutrino alerts enabling electromagnetic follow-up; Subaru/HSC deep optical follow-ups down to 25.5 mag were conducted for IceCube event 230724A, with a blind analysis including evaluation of background and true positive rates to search for tidal disruption events (TDEs).
AI.result: No TDE candidate was found in the IceCube 230724A region of interest; projections indicate that Rubin/LSST surveys could constrain TDE contributions to the neutrino background to either less than 60% (non-detection) or greater than 30% (detection) if it covers error regions of 10 neutrino events.
AI.conclusion: TDEs were not identified as sources for the IceCube 230724A neutrino event, but future wide-field surveys like Rubin/LSST can significantly constrain their role as cosmic high-energy neutrino sources.

title: Rapid quasi-periodic reconfiguration of the accretion column in pulsar 1A 0535+262
summary: Accretion onto strongly magnetized neutron stars is commonly interpreted using quasi-steady models, in which the accretion-column structure adjusts smoothly to the mass inflow rate. The cyclotron line in the X-ray spectrum, whose centroid energy traces the magnetic field strength and thus the height of the line-forming region, provides a key diagnostic of this structure. Whether this simple quasi-steady description remains valid on short dynamical timescales has remained uncertain. Here we show that, during a giant outburst of the X-ray pulsar 1A~0535+262, quasi-periodic hard X-ray flux variations are accompanied by synchronized oscillations of the cyclotron line energy, with amplitudes exceeding those expected from simple accretion-rate fluctuations. The anti-correlation between cyclotron energy and apparent flux provides direct spectral-timing evidence for rapid changes in the line-forming region, which we interpret as geometric reconfiguration of the accretion column. The variability emerges in the luminosity regime where radiation pressure becomes dynamically important. These results reveal limitations of a simple quasi-steady interpretation for this source and suggest that radiation-supported columns can enter intrinsically dynamical states in high-luminosity accreting pulsars.

AI.tldr: During a giant outburst of the X-ray pulsar 1A 0535+262, rapid synchronized oscillations in X-ray flux and cyclotron line energy reveal dynamic, radiation-pressure-driven changes in accretion column structure, challenging simple steady-state models.
AI.motivation: To investigate the validity of quasi-steady accretion models on short dynamical timescales in strongly magnetized neutron stars, specifically during high luminosity outbursts.
AI.method: Analysis of the giant outburst of the X-ray pulsar 1A 0535+262, focusing on quasi-periodic hard X-ray flux variations and corresponding oscillations in cyclotron line energy, using spectral-timing measurements.
AI.result: Discovery of synchronized oscillations in cyclotron line energy and hard X-ray flux with amplitudes greater than expected from simple accretion-rate fluctuations, showing an anti-correlation indicative of rapid geometric reconfiguration of the accretion column.
AI.conclusion: The simple quasi-steady accretion model is insufficient to explain observed rapid variability during high-luminosity states; radiation-supported accretion columns can enter dynamic states leading to rapid structural changes in accretion flows.

title: A new Chandra look at the globular cluster NGC 6540 and its peculiar X-ray flaring source
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to A&A, comments are welcome
summary: We report the results of a deep ($\approx65$ ks) Chandra observation of the globular cluster NGC 6540, obtained to investigate the nature of the peculiar X-ray source 3XMM J180608.9$-$274553. This source was previously observed with XMM$-$Newton to exhibit a short ($\approx300$ s) and intense X-ray flare whose luminosity and duration are inconsistent with both typical type I X-ray bursts from low mass X-ray binaries and stellar flares. Our new data show the presence of three faint X-ray sources near the position of the flare seen by XMM$-$Newton, only one of which was detected in a previous, much shorter Chandra observation. Based on the properties of these sources, localized at sub-arcsecond precision, and of their optical counterparts, we discuss their possible nature and association with 3XMM J180608.9$-$274553. We also discuss some scenarios to explain the X-ray flare, such as microlensing-induced amplification, black hole flaring activity analogous to that observed from Sgr A$^\ast$. Our results place new constraints on the nature of this unusual transient and highlight the power of high-resolution X-ray observations for disentangling rare phenomena in the dense stellar environments of globular clusters.

AI.tldr: Deep Chandra observations of NGC 6540 revealed multiple faint X-ray sources near an unusual transient flare position, providing new insights and constraints on its nature, with possible explanations including microlensing or black hole flares.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature of the peculiar X-ray source 3XMM J180608.9-274553 in the globular cluster NGC 6540, previously observed to exhibit an unusual X-ray flare.
AI.method: Deep (~65 ks) Chandra X-ray observations were conducted to obtain high-resolution data, allowing precise localization of faint X-ray sources near the flare position and identification of their optical counterparts.
AI.result: Three faint X-ray sources were found near the flare position, only one of which was previously detected. Analysis of source properties and optical counterparts, along with consideration of different physical scenarios, provided new constraints on the nature of the transient event.
AI.conclusion: The study constrained the origin of the unusual X-ray flare, ruling out typical explanations and suggesting possible causes such as microlensing or black hole flaring activity, demonstrating the effectiveness of high-resolution X-ray observations in resolving rare phenomena in dense stellar environments.

title: A 0.03 Hz Radio Quasi-periodic Oscillation During the 2025 Flare of GRS 1915+105
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Our weekly-cadence radio monitoring campaign captured a bright flare in 2025 from the microquasar GRS 1915+105, observed simultaneously in the S- and X-bands (2.25 GHz and 8.42 GHz) with a short single baseline of two radio telescopes in Shanghai. Through high time resolution analysis, we detected a significant and short-lived quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) at $\sim$0.03 Hz and its harmonic ($\sim$0.06 Hz) in both radio bands of two consecutive observations on MJD 60765 ($>5.9 σ$) and MJD 60772 (2.8$σ$). Crucially, the QPO frequency is identical in both radio bands and matches oscillations detected in previous years. The recurrence and wavelength independence of the QPO frequency suggest an intrinsic characteristic timescale of the accretion-jet system.

AI.tldr: High time resolution radio monitoring of GRS 1915+105 captured a flare showing a significant quasi-periodic oscillation at ~0.03 Hz and its harmonic in two radio bands, confirming it as an intrinsic timescale of the accretion-jet system.
AI.motivation: To investigate the characteristics of quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the microquasar GRS 1915+105 during a bright radio flare and understand their intrinsic origin.
AI.method: Weekly-cadence radio monitoring of GRS 1915+105 using two radio telescopes in Shanghai at S- (2.25 GHz) and X-bands (8.42 GHz) with high time resolution analysis to detect and characterize QPOs.
AI.result: Detection of a significant, short-lived QPO at approximately 0.03 Hz and its harmonic (~0.06 Hz) simultaneously in both radio bands during two observations, with identical QPO frequencies matching previous years' oscillations.
AI.conclusion: The wavelength independence and recurrence of the QPO frequency indicate it as an intrinsic characteristic timescale of the accretion-jet system in GRS 1915+105.

title: Possible High-Energy Neutrino Emission from Dark Matter Annihilation in the Disrupting Dwarf Galaxy Boötes~III
summary: We report the first search for high-energy neutrino emissions from dark matter (DM) annihilation in stellar-stream cores. Motivated by a recent gamma-ray study that proposed these cores as a new class of indirect DM targets, we analyze three stream cores in the Northern Hemisphere using the public ten-year track-like neutrino data released by IceCube. Under the $χχ\toν\barν$ annihilation hypothesis, the most significant excess among the three targets is found at the position of the nearby dwarf galaxy Boötes~III, the core of the Styx stream, with a best-fit DM mass of 26.5\,TeV. The excess has a post-trial significance of $3.1σ$. Considering the existing IceCube dwarf-galaxy limit for the same channel, we obtain a limit on the J-factor $J_{\rm ann}$, $\log_{10}(J_{\rm ann}/{\rm GeV^2\,cm^{-5}})\gtrsim 19.1^{+0.3}_{-0.5}$. This limit is broadly consistent with empirical estimates of $J_{\rm ann}$ for Boötes~III. The results provide the first candidate target with a possible HE neutrino signal associated with DM annihilation. This neutrino excess and the general existence of DM-induced neutrino signals from other similar sources will be confirmed with the near-future large high-energy neutrino detectors, thus enabling us to probe the nature of DM particles.

AI.tldr: This study is the first to search for high-energy neutrino signals from dark matter annihilation in stellar-stream cores using IceCube data, detecting a tentative neutrino excess at Boötes III related to DM annihilation, which future detectors can confirm to advance dark matter research.
AI.motivation: Stellar-stream cores have been proposed as new indirect targets for dark matter (DM) detection based on recent gamma-ray studies, motivating a search for DM-induced high-energy neutrino emissions from these sources.
AI.method: Analyzing ten years of publicly available IceCube track-like neutrino data for three stellar-stream cores in the Northern Hemisphere, testing the DM annihilation channel χχ→νν̄, and searching for neutrino excesses potentially associated with these sources.
AI.result: The most significant neutrino excess was found at Boötes III, the core of the Styx stream, with a best-fit DM mass of 26.5 TeV, showing a post-trial significance of 3.1σ. A limit on the J-factor for DM annihilation was derived, consistent with empirical estimates for Boötes III.
AI.conclusion: This work presents the first candidate high-energy neutrino signal from DM annihilation in a stellar-stream core, providing a new target for indirect DM searches. Future large neutrino detectors will validate this signal and enhance our understanding of DM particle properties.

title: Fast radio bursts, magnetars and earthquakes: their "family feud"?
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in Science China Physics, Mechanics & Astronomy
summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration cosmic transients whose origin remains elusive. Competing models invoke either earthquake-like processes or flare-like mechanisms. To discriminate between these scenarios, we develop a novel diagnostic, the Pincus-Lyapunov diagram (PLD), to characterize the energetic transients in the stochasticity-chaos phase space. We compile burst sequences from five representative FRBs (FRB 20121102A, FRB 20190520B, FRB 20201124A, FRB 20220912A, and FRB 20240114A), together with those from magnetar flares (SGR J1550$-$5418, SGR J0501+4516, SGR 1806$-$20, SGR 1900+14, and SGR J1935+2154), pulsar glitches, solar flares, and earthquakes, and map them onto the PLD for comparative analysis. The resulting diagram shows that FRBs occupy a distinct region of the phase space. Specifically, a permutation test reveals a statistically significant difference in the distributions of magnetar flares and pulsar glitches compared to those of repeating FRBs ($p$-value $\simeq 0.05$). To examine whether temporal variations in source activity can shift a repeater's position in this phase space, we analyze the time evolution of the most prolific repeater, FRB~20240114A. For this repeating FRB, both Pincus Index and Lyapunov Exponent demonstrate statistically stable behaviour over the eight-month observation session, with Augmented Dickey--Fuller tests yielding $p \simeq 1.78\times10^{-3}$ and $9.91\times10^{-3}$, respectively. By assembling the most comprehensive dataset to date, our work indicates that the trigger mechanisms of repeating FRBs are likely to be distinct from those driving magnetar flares, pulsar glitches, solar flares, and earthquakes.

AI.tldr: This study introduces the Pincus-Lyapunov diagram as a novel diagnostic to distinguish the origins of fast radio bursts. Analysis of multiple FRBs and other astrophysical phenomena reveals that repeating FRBs occupy a unique parameter space, implying their trigger mechanisms differ from magnetar flares, pulsar glitches, solar flares, and earthquakes.
AI.motivation: The origin of fast radio bursts (FRBs) is unclear, with competing models suggesting either earthquake-like or flare-like mechanisms. To resolve this uncertainty, a diagnostic tool is needed to differentiate between these scenarios.
AI.method: The study develops the Pincus-Lyapunov diagram (PLD) to analyze energetic transients in a stochasticity-chaos phase space. It compiles burst sequences from five representative FRBs and various astrophysical and geophysical phenomena (magnetar flares, pulsar glitches, solar flares, earthquakes) to map and compare their behavior on the PLD. Statistical tests including permutation and Augmented Dickey-Fuller tests are applied to assess differences and stability.
AI.result: FRBs occupy a distinct region in the stochasticity-chaos phase space separate from magnetar flares, pulsar glitches, solar flares, and earthquakes. The distributions of magnetar flares and pulsar glitches differ significantly from those of repeating FRBs. Temporal analysis of the most prolific repeater, FRB 20240114A, shows stable behavior over time in Pincus Index and Lyapunov Exponent values.
AI.conclusion: The trigger mechanisms of repeating FRBs are likely distinct from those driving magnetar flares, pulsar glitches, solar flares, and earthquakes, supporting the idea that FRBs have unique origins differing from previously competing models.

title: Locating the Production Sites of High-Energy Neutrinos in Blazar Jets
comment: 19 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables, submitted to ApJ. Suggestions, comments or feedback will be appreciated!
summary: The production sites of high-energy neutrinos in blazar jets remain poorly constrained. In this work, we investigate the physical conditions required for efficient neutrino production by combining radio-constrained jet properties with multi-zone emission modeling. We show that efficient neutrino production requires an external radiation field stronger than the magnetic field in the jet frame. This environment not only enhances the efficiency of photohadronic interactions but also suppresses synchrotron radiation from secondary pairs, thereby avoiding overshooting the hard X-ray data. Such conditions can be achieved in regions near or within the broad-line region. However, assuming a single emission zone, these conditions are generally inconsistent with the double-bump flux ratio of the observed broadband emission. This implies that the neutrino-emitting region should be physically separated from the dominant electromagnetic emission zone. We further show that such a scenario can be realized either if the jet completes its acceleration within sub-parsec scales or if the bulk Lorentz factor is intrinsically large, both of which appear uncommon based on current observations. These results provide a natural explanation for the rarity of blazar-neutrino associations and highlight the importance of constraining jet structure at small scales to identify promising neutrino-emitting blazars.

AI.tldr: The study shows that efficient high-energy neutrino production in blazars requires specific jet conditions with external radiation fields and spatially separate emission regions, explaining the rarity of neutrino-blazar links and emphasizing the need for detailed small-scale jet structure studies.
AI.motivation: To better understand the physical conditions and locations within blazar jets that are responsible for high-energy neutrino production, which currently remain poorly constrained.
AI.method: Combined radio-constrained jet properties with multi-zone emission modeling to investigate the requirements for efficient neutrino production.
AI.result: Found that efficient neutrino production requires an external radiation field stronger than the magnetic field in the jet frame, typically near or within the broad-line region, but this is inconsistent with the observed broadband emission if assuming a single emission zone. Concluded that the neutrino-emitting region must be physically separated from the main electromagnetic emission zone. This separation is plausible if the jet accelerates within sub-parsec scales or has a large bulk Lorentz factor, both of which are rare observationally.
AI.conclusion: The rarity of blazar-neutrino associations can be explained by the need for specific jet conditions and separate neutrino emission zones, highlighting the significance of detailed jet structure constraints at small scales to identify potential neutrino-producing blazars.

title: Revealing the high redshift host galaxy of the short GRB 061201 with JWST
summary: Using deep near-infrared and optical images from JWST and HST, we identify a new host galaxy candidate for GRB 061201. It lies ~2" from the optical afterglow position. Photometric redshift fitting yields z~1.2. We compare the previously proposed host at z=0.111 with the new candidate. The chance-coincidence probability is $P_{cc}=0.18$, above the classical threshold of 0.1 but consistent with a physical association given the extreme depth of JWST imaging. In contrast, evaluated with corresponding JWST observations, the previously claimed host has a lower $P_{cc}=0.11$, which is driven primarily by bright-tail statistics rather than a more plausible association. A high-z origin is favored by three independent lines of evidence. First, for the z=0.111 scenario, the beaming-corrected energy shows GRB 061201 is an outlier of the Ghirlanda ($E_{p,i}-E_γ$) relation for short GRBs, while for the z=1.2 scenario, it is well consistent with the Amati relation. Second, deep near-infrared observations rule out a kilonova similar to AT2017gfo at z=0.111. Third, afterglow modeling yields an AIC criterion of $Δ$AIC=16.35, providing strong evidence for the high-redshift scenario. Assuming the host candidate is the actual host galaxy of GRB 061201, the physical offset is 16.4-16.9 kpc (substantially reduced from ~42 kpc) and the host stellar age is ~2 Gyr, which are consistent with the host population of short GRBs. A low-redshift origin would lead to a very high binary neutron star merger rate of ~1400 Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$, which is contradictory to the gravitational-wave constraint. We suggest that GRB 061201 originates from a moderately high-redshift (z~1.2) host, significantly alleviating this apparent merger rate discrepancy. This case demonstrates the power of deep JWST exposures in revealing the host galaxies of historically hostless GRBs.

AI.tldr: Deep JWST imaging reveals a new likely host galaxy for GRB 061201 at z~1.2, resolving previous host ambiguity and merger rate conflicts, highlighting JWST's capability in studying hostless GRBs.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ambiguous host galaxy association of GRB 061201 and address the inconsistency in neutron star merger rates implied by a low-redshift host.
AI.method: Utilized deep near-infrared and optical imaging from JWST and HST to identify host candidates and conducted photometric redshift fitting, chance-coincidence probability analysis, GRB energy relation comparisons, kilonova exclusion through infrared observations, and afterglow modeling with AIC criterion.
AI.result: The newly identified candidate at z~1.2 aligns with GRB energy relations, lacks kilonova signatures at low redshift, yields strong statistical support from afterglow modeling, matches typical short GRB host properties, and alleviates merger rate tension with gravitational wave observations.
AI.conclusion: GRB 061201 likely originates from a moderately high-redshift (z~1.2) host galaxy identified using deep JWST data, resolving previous discrepancies in host association and merger rates.

title: Statistical properties of type-II bursts in Rapid Burster observed with Insight-HXMT
comment: 16 pages, 11 figures, published online in Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
summary: We report the detection of type-II X-ray bursts in a neutron star low mass X-ray binary MXB 1730-335 (also known as Rapid Burster) observed with Insight- HXMT satellite. We found significant variations in the burst properties along with the decay phases of its 2017 and 2020 outbursts, such as switches between different burst modes.We investigated the statistical distributions of burst parameters (peak flux $F_{\mathrm{peak}}$, fluence $E$, burst duration $t_{\mathrm{dur}}$, recurrence time $Δt$) and studied their correlations.We confirm the relaxation oscillator behavior ($E \propto Δt^α$), and find that for mode-2 bursts the index $α$ is around 1. For mode-1 bursts, $α$ varies with $Δt$ and the $E-Δt^α$ relation can be described by a broken powerlaw model.We also confirm that $F_{\mathrm{peak}}$ is correlated with $E$ below a critical value and is independent of $Δt$.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes Insight-HXMT observations of type-II X-ray bursts from MXB 1730-335, revealing distinct burst mode behaviors and statistical correlations, confirming relaxation oscillator relations, and refining models of energy-recurrence time correlations.
AI.motivation: To understand the variable burst behaviors and underlying physics of type-II X-ray bursts in the Rapid Burster, specifically the statistical properties and correlations of burst parameters across different burst modes and outburst phases.
AI.method: The authors analyzed data from the Insight-HXMT satellite observing the 2017 and 2020 outbursts of MXB 1730-335, performing statistical analysis on burst parameter distributions and their correlations, including application of broken power-law modeling.
AI.result: Significant variations in burst properties and mode switches were observed during outbursts. For mode-2 bursts, the energy-recurrence time correlation follows a power-law with index approximately 1. For mode-1 bursts, the correlation is better described by a broken power-law. Peak flux correlates with fluence below a critical threshold and is not dependent on recurrence time.
AI.conclusion: The paper confirms the relaxation oscillator behavior in type-II X-ray bursts from MXB 1730-335, characterizes differences between burst modes, and identifies correlations among burst parameters.

title: Regression on Regression: Mapping Data-Driven Binary Black Hole Merger Rate Fits to Progenitor Histories
summary: The binary black hole (BBH) merger rate is governed by the progenitor formation rate and the distribution of delay-times between formation and merger, but these functions remain poorly constrained. We introduce a framework that maps the parameters of physics-driven models directly onto existing data-driven fits of the BBH merger rate. This ``regression on regression'' approach enables physical interpretation of flexible population models without the computational burden of reanalyzing the underlying gravitational-wave event data. Applying this method to the \textsc{B-Spline} merger-rate posteriors from the Fourth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, we fit the minimum delay time ($τ_{\text{min}}$), delay-time power-law index ($α$), and progenitor formation parameters controlling the normalization ($\mathcal{A}$), early-time growth ($γ$), and late-time decay ($δ$). Increasing the number of anchoring redshift points from two to four reduces the median sum-squared error (SSE) by a factor of $\approx 4.5$. However, residuals reveal that the physical model does not pass through all four anchors, exposing model misspecification and demonstrating a key strength of the framework: unlike standard inference methods, which preferentially weight compatible curves and mask underlying tensions, our approach exposes BBH posteriors irreconcilable with the model. Despite uncertainties at $z\gtrsim1$, the shape of the progenitor formation rate at low-$z$ is robust and evolves more steeply than the global star formation rate (SFR), supporting a preference for low metallicity environments. Specifically, the log-space slope of the progenitor rate is $\approx 5.3$ times steeper than the SFR between $z=0.1$ and $z=1.0$. Ultimately, a more complex phenomenological model is required to match the \textsc{B-Spline} merger rates.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a regression framework mapping physics-based BBH merger models onto data-driven fits, revealing current model limitations and showing the progenitor formation rate evolves more steeply than star formation at low redshifts, implying low metallicity preference.
AI.motivation: The binary black hole (BBH) merger rate depends on poorly constrained progenitor formation rates and delay-time distributions.
AI.method: They introduced a 'regression on regression' framework that fits physics-driven model parameters directly onto data-driven BBH merger rate fits from gravitational-wave catalogs, avoiding costly reanalysis of raw data.
AI.result: Applying this method to B-Spline merger rate posteriors, they estimated parameters controlling delay times and progenitor formation, finding the physical model insufficient to fit all anchor points, revealing model misspecification. The progenitor formation rate at low redshift is steeper than the global star formation rate, indicating preference for low metallicity environments.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates the utility of their regression framework in exposing model-data tensions and concludes that more complex phenomenological models are needed to accurately represent BBH merger rates.
